title: Turn a legacy system's Y/N and 1/0 flags into Booleans
examObjective: Converting between output types and data types using DataWeave
basics: `as Boolean` converts only the text "true" and "false". Other ways of writing yes and no, such as "Y" or "1", need your own rule. `contains` checks whether an Array holds a value: `["Y", "1"] contains "Y"` is true.
prompt:
A legacy system exports flags in whatever form each screen used: `"Y"`/`"N"`, `"y"`/`"n"`, `"1"`/`"0"`, the Numbers `1`/`0`, or `"TRUE"`/`"false"`.

Return each flag as a Boolean: `true` for Y, 1 and true in any case, `false` for everything else.
hints: `"Y" as Boolean` fails. You need your own list of values that mean yes.
Normalise before comparing: the same flag arrives in upper case, lower case, and as a Number.
solution:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map (["Y", "1", "TRUE"] contains upper($ as String))

mustFail.why: compares case-sensitively, so a lower-case y is read as no
mustFail.script:
%dw 2.0
output application/json
---
payload map (["Y", "1", "TRUE", "true"] contains ($ as String))

mustFail.why: does not convert the value to text first, so the Number 1 is not found in a list of Strings

explanation.approach: A lookup of the values that mean yes is clearer than a chain of comparisons. The value has to be normalised first: converting to String makes the Number 1 and the text "1" the same, and upper-casing makes "y" and "Y" the same.

snippets.label: A Number is not found among Strings
snippets.note: `contains` compares type as well as value.
